official.name: German
official.note: small community near the eastern border

terrainDescription.zh: 北部法蘭德斯為低地平原，南部瓦隆地區的阿登高地地形起伏較大，北海沿岸有一小段海岸線。
terrainDescription.en: Flanders in the north is low-lying plain, the Ardennes uplands in southern Wallonia are hillier, and a short North Sea coastline runs along the northwest.

plate.color: white background, red text — the only EU country using red-on-white rather than black-on-white/yellow; plate is tied to the owner/driver, not the vehicle

roadInfra.bollardStyle: Distinctive white bollard with a yellow rectangle

utilityPole.transformerMount: Poles closely resemble France's ladder/waffle-style concrete poles

historicalContext.zh: 比利時三種官方語言依地區單一使用：法蘭德斯用荷蘭語、瓦隆用法語、東部小區域用德語；僅布魯塞爾首都區官方雙語（Brussel/Bruxelles 並列），其餘地區路牌只會顯示當地語言的地名，不會雙語並列——這點常被誤解。
historicalContext.en: Belgium's three official languages are used regionally, not uniformly: Dutch in Flanders, French in Wallonia, German in a small eastern pocket. Only the Brussels-Capital Region is officially bilingual (Brussel/Bruxelles shown together) — road signs elsewhere show only the local region's language, a commonly misunderstood point.
